# Test-process candidate only. Do not install this in the production editor.
func _clip_set_probe_prepare(target: StringName) -> void:
	if not has_meta(&"clip_set_probe_enabled"):
		return
	var player := animation_player
	assert(player.get_animation_library_list().size() == 1)
	assert(player.playback_default_blend_time == 0.0 and player.get_queue().is_empty())
	var library := player.get_animation_library(&"")
	var full: Dictionary = get_meta(&"clip_set_probe_full", {})
	var stubs: Dictionary = get_meta(&"clip_set_probe_stubs", {})
	if full.is_empty():
		for clip: StringName in player.get_animation_list():
			assert(player.animation_get_next(clip) == &"")
			var source := library.get_animation(clip)
			full[clip] = source
			var stub := Animation.new()
			stub.length = source.length
			stub.step = source.step
			stub.loop_mode = source.loop_mode
			stubs[clip] = stub
		set_meta(&"clip_set_probe_full", full)
		set_meta(&"clip_set_probe_stubs", stubs)
	# Never replace the assigned clip: its current playback must stay intact.
	# Keep the incoming clip, previous clip, idle and any authored RESET.
	for clip: StringName in full:
		var required: bool = clip in [target, player.assigned_animation, &"idle", &"RESET"]
		if "--clip-resident" in OS.get_cmdline_user_args() and clip in [&"walk_slash", &"guard"]: required = true
		var source: Animation = full[clip] if required else stubs[clip]
		if library.get_animation(clip) != source:
			assert(library.add_animation(clip, source) == OK)
